source.snippet: "My website is getting thousands of hits a day from bots searching for WordPress vulnerabilities. I do NOT run WordPress, and the site is on shared hosting, so I don't have backend access. I added RedirectMatch 301 /wp to my .htaccess... but the attempts still fill my log with tons of crap."

problem_statement: Small website owners on shared hosting are inundated with bot traffic probing for WordPress vulnerabilities they don't even use, polluting logs, inflating analytics, and wasting server resources — with no easy backend firewall access to stop it.
target_segment: Small business owners and independent webmasters on shared hosting plans who lack server-level access to configure firewalls or bot-blocking rules.
notes: Moderate buyer signal: shared-hosting customers do pay monthly for hosting and pay for tools/plugins that solve security problems. The frustration is clear and repeated (also echoed in the serverfault iptables item about BingBot alerting 'AI friends and hackers'). A managed bot-blocking service or .htaccess rule generator tuned for non-WordPress shared-hosting sites could command a small SaaS fee. Pain is real but individual ticket volume is low — combined signal from two independent posts raises confidence slightly.
